Estimate selection coefficient from frequency trajectory

Source: R/selection.R
estimateSelectionCoefficient.Rd

Given a vector of allele frequencies observed over equally-spaced time points, estimates the selection coefficient \(s\) using the change in logit-transformed frequency per unit time: $$s = \frac{\Delta \mathrm{logit}(p)}{\Delta t}$$ where \(\mathrm{logit}(p) = \log(p / (1 - p))\).

Usage

estimateSelectionCoefficient(freqs, times = NULL, generation_time = 1)

Arguments

freqs

Numeric vector. Allele frequencies at successive time points (values must be in (0, 1)).

times

Numeric vector (optional). Time values for each observation. If NULL, integer time steps 1, 2, ... are used.

generation_time

Numeric scalar. Time per generation (default: 1). Used to scale the selection coefficient.

Value

Numeric vector of selection coefficient estimates, one per consecutive time interval. Length is length(freqs) - 1.

Details

This assumes a simple deterministic selection model. Each consecutive pair of time points yields one estimate of \(s\).

References

Feder AF et al. (2016). More effective drugs lead to harder selective sweeps in the evolution of drug resistance in HIV-1. eLife 5:e10670. doi:10.7554/eLife.10670

Examples

freqs <- c(0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50)
estimateSelectionCoefficient(freqs)
#> [1] 0.7472144 1.0986123 1.0986123
estimateSelectionCoefficient(freqs, times = c(0, 3, 7, 14))
#> [1] 0.2490715 0.2746531 0.1569446
